terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Cast concrete, fixed in the ground: nothing opens, turns or swings, nothing attaches, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract. Scattered across open ground in parks and school yards, so the two draw calls are the design constraint. Parks, school yards and temple grounds; the slab a warm buff aggregate of cream, tan, dark-grey and brown stones, the base plain grey concrete darkening under the slab.

reasoning: TWO components on TWO materials, one merge each: the terrazzo SLAB (one box) and the CONCRETE base (sub-plate, pedestal, footing block, chamfered cap and four corner pads merged). Two draw calls of two.

Two materials because one roughness cannot be both: the ground-and-polished aggregate slab reads 0.62 with soft stone highlights, the cast concrete 0.92 and dead matte. Both WHITE with the tones as vertex colours; the slab tone multiplies into a pebble canvas, the concrete carries a light grime canvas.
No repetition system: four pads are four boxes inside the base merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one declared box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is three chunky closed volumes in a T -- a thin square slab wider than anything under it, a slender square post, a broad low plinth -- and the aggregate on the slab. A round slab or a tapered post would be a different table; a flat-coloured slab would be a concrete bench.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: Four-fold symmetric in plan: the proxy measures identical width and depth and the plate shows one plain cast face per elevation, so the two hidden elevations are built as the two visible ones.
The base notches are corner pads, not a channel: the proxy's bottom row is solid at both ends and hollow across the middle, and the plate shows two rectangular notches on the front face.

The pedestal's darker read in the plate (luma 117-123 against the footing's 158) is the slab's cast shadow, not a second concrete: one tone, with a y-axis vertex tint from white at the footing top to 0.78 under the slab standing in for the shadow the harness does not cast.
The declared plan was corrected 0.70 -> 0.62 on the proxy before building (arithmetic in envelopeDerivation).
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.62 x 0.72 x 0.62 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: the table envelope. The shipped compound is DERIVED from the geometry by scripts/derive-colliders.mjs.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: Four-fold symmetric in plan: the proxy measures identical width and depth and the plate shows one plain cast face per elevation, so the two hidden elevations are built as the two visible ones.
The base notches are corner pads, not a channel: the proxy's bottom row is solid at both ends and hollow across the middle, and the plate shows two rectangular notches on the front face.

The pedestal's darker read in the plate (luma 117-123 against the footing's 158) is the slab's cast shadow, not a second concrete: one tone, with a y-axis vertex tint from white at the footing top to 0.78 under the slab standing in for the shadow the harness does not cast.
The declared plan was corrected 0.70 -> 0.62 on the proxy before building (arithmetic in envelopeDerivation).

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows).

silhouette.description: A 0.62 m square slab 0.050 thick at 0.670-0.720 on a 0.59 m concrete sub-plate 0.015 thick, over a 0.23 m square post from 0.094 to 0.655, standing on a 0.365 m square footing 0.078 tall whose top 23 mm chamfers in to 0.86 of its plan, on four 0.11 m corner pads 16 mm tall.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z +-0.310 at the slab, y 0 to 0.720 at the slab top. The LIST-TIME declaration was 0.70 x 0.72 x 0.70 (w/h 0.972). The Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox 1.636 x 1.903 x 1.636, w/h = d/h = 0.860 with a square plan. Height is the trustworthy axis for a table -- a park table sits at dining height -- so the plan is 0.72 x 0.860 = 0.619 -> 0.62 m and the declaration was corrected on both plan axes before building. Stack read off the proxy in fractions of H: slab rows 0.91-1.00 (0.065 m, the lowest row a shade narrower, which is the sub-plate), pedestal rows 0.14-0.89 at 30 of 80 columns = 0.375 W = 0.23 m square, footing rows 0.02-0.13 at 47 columns = 0.59 W = 0.365 m square with its top two rows stepping in (a chamfer) and row 0.00 solid at the ends and hollow in the middle (the plate's notched base -- corner pads). The plate settles the split of the 0.065: the slab face measures 60 px against the 260 px pedestal (0.23 m), so 0.050 of terrazzo on a 0.015 concrete sub-plate.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.636 x 1.903 x 1.636, w/h = d/h = 0.860, which is what corrected the declared plan from 0.70 to 0.62. Every station above is the proxy band table read in fractions of H; the plate only split the slab from its sub-plate.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the prop is four-fold symmetric in plan on the proxy (w/h = d/h to three decimals) and every visible elevation is the same plain cast face.

componentTree.name: Pebble-wash terrazzo slab
componentTree.topologyRationale: One box on one material: one draw call. The aggregate is a canvas, not geometry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Box 0.62 x 0.050 x 0.62 from 0.670 to 0.720, world UVs at 0.35 m so the stones repeat at real size across the top and down the edges.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The slab's underside meets the sub-plate's top as an OPPOSED butt joint. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A near-white vertex tone multiplied into the pebble canvas, which carries the colour.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the table envelope. The shipped compound is DERIVED from the geometry by scripts/derive-colliders.mjs.

componentTree.name: Cast concrete pedestal, sub-plate and stepped footing
componentTree.topologyRationale: Sub-plate, post, footing block, four pads and the chamfered cap merged into one geometry on one material: one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Sub-plate 0.59 x 0.015 at 0.655-0.670; post 0.23 square from 0.089 to 0.660 (embedded 5 mm into both neighbours); footing 0.365 square from 0.016 to 0.074 with a frustum cap to 0.094 stepping in to 0.86 of the plan; four 0.11 pads 0-0.021 set 0.02 in from the footing corners.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The post runs 5 mm INTO the sub-plate above and the footing below, the pads 5 mm up into the footing, and the chamfer frustum starts 3 mm down inside the footing block at 2 mm less than its plan, so no bounding-box face shares a plane with a co-facing neighbour. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 0.60 m and a y-axis tint.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: One concrete tone as a vertex colour, a y tint for the slab's shadow, a light grime canvas.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/slab-top.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.809. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/slab-top.png -- pebble-wash aggregate over the slab top and edges

evidence: Measured on the plate: slab top #c0ab95 / #bca896 / #c0a990 (luma 172-175), analyze_texture meanLum 167.8 sat 0.256 mottle 0.134; extract_pbr_evidence palette #BAA189 #A48C74 #CEB79E #E5D0B8 #87705B at confidence 0.809. Stones 5-10 px across on an 830 px slab with a few at 25, i.e. 4-8 mm with some at 20.

Textureless as DECLARED: the aggregate is a 512 px pebble canvas bound AFTER construction (buff cement ground, 2600 stones of 4-16 px in seven measured tones with a highlight crescent each), repeating at 0.35 m through world UVs. Probed on the render: vertex tone 0xf4eee6 over ground (0.72, 0.64, 0.53) lands the slab top at luma 172 against the plate's 175.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: Measured on the plate: footing front #a39e94 (158) and footing top #b3ada3 (174); pedestal #7a746a / #807b6f (117-123) in the slab's shadow, analyze_texture worn-composite roughness 0.9 on both crops; extract_pbr_evidence palette #A29D93 #A6A198 #59544C #9D998F #ADA89F at confidence 0.86 (footing) and 0.832 (pedestal).

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90. 108/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two canvases, factory in 130 ms.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: terrazzo and concrete: 2 of 2; every tone within each is a vertex colour.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 108 of 2000: seven boxes and one frustum.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes for the slab, sub-plate, post, footing and pads; a frustum for the footing's chamfered cap.
No InstancedMesh at two draw calls. In a scene the HOST instances the table.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two canvases after construction -- a 512 px pebble tile on the terrazzo (1.0 MB) and a 256 px grime tile on the concrete -- the factory built in 130 ms.

risks.description: The list-time plan of 0.70 disagreed with the proxy's 0.860 aspect by 13%.
risks.mitigation: Corrected to 0.62 on the height axis before building, arithmetic recorded on the asset notes and in envelopeDerivation.

risks.description: A pebble canvas can read as marbles or as noise depending on stone size against tile size.
risks.mitigation: First render at 1500 stones of up to 30 px read as marbles; re-authored at 2600 stones of 4-16 px on a 0.35 m tile, which matches the plate's 5-10 px on an 830 px slab.

risks.description: The harness casts no shadow, so the pedestal would render as bright as the footing where the plate shows it 35 levels darker.
risks.mitigation: A y-axis vertex tint from white at the footing top to 0.78 under the slab.
